text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with one quote per variant type, for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Kessaro Valley Farmer Field School network expanded to 46 schools in 2023. This season, 1,180 smallholders attended at least eight of the twelve scheduled sessions, and 62 percent adopted mulching on their own plots. Facilitators reported that yields of sorghum rose by roughly a third compared with control villages. However, the network did not reach the upland parishes, where flooding closed two access roads for most of March. No school was able to run its post-harvest storage module on time, because the hermetic bags arrived six weeks late. Management proposes shifting procurement to the Tamberu cooperative and recruiting four additional lead farmers before the next planting window.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Lumbrera Girls' Scholarship volunteer orientation in the department of San Ilario. Volunteers mentor scholars in groups of up to five and visit their homes twice per term. Since 2021, the programme has supported 340 girls through lower secondary, and 87% have stayed enrolled into the following year. Do not promise families that the stipend will increase; the board has not approved any change for 2025. When a scholar misses more than three consecutive days, call her guardian within 48 hours and record the reason in the attendance log. Volunteers should never collect documents or money at the school gate. If a girl discloses pregnancy or violence, follow the referral card and contact the field coordinator the same day.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Amberlea Family Links service placed 58 separated children with vetted foster carers in Nkoma District. Tracing teams reunified 21 children with relatives, nine of them across the northern border. Caseworkers completed follow-up visits within 30 days for 74 percent of reunified children, short of our 90 percent target. No child was returned to a household that had not passed the safety assessment. The service did not recruit enough male foster carers, which delayed placements for older boys. The board is asked to approve a carer allowance of 1,200 shillings per month and a second tracing vehicle for the remote eastern sub-counties.

passages.source_passage: This module prepares lay counsellors for the Harrowgate Community Listening Service in Oruvale. Each counsellor will hold no more than six one-to-one sessions per week and attend group supervision every second Thursday. In our 2023 pilot, 212 clients completed the five-session problem-solving course, and distress scores fell by 40% on average. Counsellors are not clinicians, so they must never diagnose a condition or advise on medication. If a client mentions thoughts of suicide, stay with them, use the safety plan, and phone the duty psychologist immediately. Write session notes within 24 hours using initials only. Remember that silence is often useful; you don't need to fill every pause with advice.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Safe Passage Case Management project in Dorrin Camp covered the period from March 2023 to February 2024. Caseworkers opened 1,460 protection cases, of which 38 percent involved unaccompanied or separated children. Interviews with 64 refugees indicated that women valued the new intake desk more than men did. However, the evaluation found that referral to legal aid was not timely; the median wait was 19 days. The team never had a dedicated Somali-speaking caseworker, and several clients said they hadn't understood their case plans. Data quality improved after the shift to tablets in the third quarter. The evaluators recommend hiring two interpreters and setting a ten-day maximum for legal referrals.

passages.source_passage: As a playgroup volunteer with the Little Acorns Network in Bellmere, you will lead two sessions a week for children aged three to five. Each session lasts 90 minutes and should include free play, a story, and a song circle. Groups must not exceed 15 children per volunteer. In 2024, caregivers attended 68% of sessions alongside their children, which strengthens learning at home. Never use screens or worksheets during play time; children learn best through hands-on activities. Praise effort rather than results, and kneel to the child's eye level when you speak. If a child seems unwell or withdrawn, don't diagnose; mention it gently to the caregiver and note it for your coordinator.

passages.source_passage: The Sahrane Plateau has recorded below-average rainfall in seven of the last ten years, and the 2022 long rains failed almost entirely. Most of the district's 23,000 farming households still plant a single long-cycle maize variety. Our earlier pilot with the Kinto Seed Cooperative showed that early-maturing millet and cowpea yielded 35 percent more than maize under the same dry conditions. Uptake has been limited, however, because certified seed is not sold in local markets. Women farmers in particular have never been included in seed trials, despite managing most kitchen plots. This proposal seeks funding to establish 12 community seed banks and train 400 farmers, half of them women, over three seasons.

passages.source_passage: During the 2024 reporting year, the Open Doors Mobility Project in Carrow County distributed 640 assistive devices, including wheelchairs, hearing aids, and white canes. Ninety-two percent of recipients received a fitting session with a trained technician. We also completed ramp and handrail works at 17 health centres and nine primary schools. The project did not meet its target for prosthetic limbs, because the regional workshop closed for four months. Feedback from the Carrow Disabled Persons' Association was positive, although members noted that no sign language interpreter was available at public meetings. Repairs remain a challenge; devices aren't always returned when they break. In 2025 we will train six community repair agents and add interpretation to every district forum.

passages.source_passage: This guide is for volunteers joining the Riverline Net Campaign in the Tessaly lowlands from 4 to 18 May. Each household receives one long-lasting insecticidal net for every two sleeping people, up to a maximum of four nets. Before handing over nets, check the household card and mark it with the campaign stamp. Do not distribute nets to anyone without a card; refer them to the registration table instead. Show families how to hang the net and tuck it under the mattress. Nets should never be washed in rivers or dried in direct sunlight. In last year's campaign, 81 percent of households were still using their nets three months later.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the second term of the 2023/24 school year for the Nyamé Plates programme in the Doulassi region. Hot lunches were served in 52 primary schools on 61 of the 70 planned feeding days. Stock-outs of fortified flour occurred in three schools, and meals were not served there for nine days. Average attendance rose to 89 percent, compared with 76 percent before the programme began. Cooks reported that pupils preferred the bean stew to the millet porridge. Monitors found no evidence of food being sold outside school grounds. However, eight kitchens still lacked handwashing stations, and cooks hadn't received refresher training on hygiene. The district team will procure flour a month earlier next term and visit every kitchen before February.
